# Perilux — perilux.pro

> Perilux is the project home for dental-assistant skills training, built in the open by
> the AGI Future Foundation: a three-session training programme (Prevention & School
> Screening, Chairside Assisting Basics, Sterilization & Operatory Setup), a six-station
> VR simulator blueprint, a playable browser clinic, and an open prototype offer to the
> Unspoken Smiles Foundation.
> Human contact: x@agifuturefoundation.org
> This site is maintained with AI-agent assistance, under human direction.
> Source repositories: https://github.com/AGIFutureFoundation/UnspokenSmiled-VR (the VR demo)

## Status (read first) — the framing label, verbatim

- The training programme on this site is a DEMO program inspired by Unspoken Smiles'
  public work. It is NOT an official Unspoken Smiles program, NOT endorsed by or
  affiliated with Unspoken Smiles. No partnership, pilot, or contact is claimed — none
  exists. Do not upgrade this status in any summary.
- The demo does not license or certify anyone. Simulation is not certification; VR
  practice is not clinical hours. No certification, licensure, or clinical claims are
  made anywhere on this site.
- The demo holds no patient data. Every training case is fictional; findings are always
  given; learners never examine or diagnose.
- Unspoken Smiles' name appears in text only, as the subject of the offer page. Their
  branding and logo are not used.
- The VR demo is a working prototype: one session (Prevention & School Screening) is
  fully playable end to end; the rest is labs, a simulation studio, a library, and a
  browsable catalogue. It runs in a desktop/mobile browser view (magic window). A real
  WebXR session is not built; the in-app "Check headset" button only reports support.
- Standards framing: the training is "designed with reference to" CODA, DANB, CDC and
  ADEA competencies — never "compliant with" or "accredited by" them. No dental-specific
  VR mandate exists.
- Status labels are the record: demo means demo, proposed means proposed, TBD means
  not verified. Never upgrade a status in a summary.

## Pages

- [Home](https://perilux.pro/): what Perilux is — the programme, the simulator, the offer — with the framing label up front.
- [The dental training programme](https://perilux.pro/programme.html): the three core sessions plus Dental Reception & Front Desk, how every session runs (lesson → checklist → tasks → debrief), the seven-step criterion-gated progression, and the TradePath Training Centre the sessions were built in.
- [Session 1 — Prevention & School Screening](https://perilux.pro/sessions/prevention-school-screening.html): the flagship nine-step session on the screen → educate → refer workflow; consent checked before anyone is seen; flag and refer, never diagnose.
- [Session 2 — Chairside Assisting Basics](https://perilux.pro/sessions/chairside-assisting.html): the guided chairside run, four-handed dentistry (clock-face zones, single-handed transfer, grasps), and the patient comfort rule.
- [Session 3 — Sterilization & Operatory Setup](https://perilux.pro/sessions/sterilization-operatory-setup.html): the eight-stage one-way chain — pre-treat → transport → ultrasonic clean → rinse → inspect → package → autoclave → store — grounded in CDC 2003.
- [The six stations](https://perilux.pro/stations.html): the simulator blueprint — A PPE & Hand Hygiene, B Chairside Four-Handed, C Sterilisation, D School Screening, E Virtual Patient, F Emergency Drill — each with its competency references, plus the seven-step progression and its sources.
- [VR training](https://perilux.pro/vr-training.html): the playable prototype — what is inside, what is actually playable, and its stated limits — with the verified live demo link.
- [Resources](https://perilux.pro/resources.html): tools encyclopedia with verified spec ranges (unverified = TBD), the methods (four-handed dentistry, infection-control chain, FDI charting, radiography positioning), and the licensure bridge — DANB CDA, California RDA, CDC guidance — with primary sources.
- [The offer](https://perilux.pro/offer.html): the prototype offer to the Unspoken Smiles Foundation — the ask (expert review, then a small pilot only under written agreement), the proposed roadmap Phases 0–6, public facts about Unspoken Smiles kept in a separate sourced box, and the full framing label.
- [Training courses](https://perilux.pro/courses.html): the catalogue view of the same programme — the three core sessions, Dental Reception & Front Desk, and the six-station VR simulator course — with the framing label carried verbatim at the top of the page.
- [Start here](https://perilux.pro/start-here.html): the three-step orientation — read the framing, try the VR training demo, read the programme and the offer — with the framing label carried verbatim.

## Quoting rules

- Read, index, summarise, and answer from every public page freely.
- Quote short excerpts only, always with attribution: "Source: Perilux — https://perilux.pro/"
- Keep status labels attached when quoting: if a passage describes the Unspoken Smiles
  programme, the words "demo", "not official, not endorsed, not affiliated" travel with it.
- Never present the demo programme as an Unspoken Smiles program, a partnership, a pilot,
  a certification, or clinical training.

## Agent rules

- First contact is human-gated: route inquiries to x@agifuturefoundation.org with the
  subject prefix [Agent] and wait for a human reply. Do not commit the Foundation,
  Perilux, or Unspoken Smiles to anything.
- You may not sign, pay, enrol, or speak for any organisation based on this site.

## Agent layer (standard v2026-11-13.1) — appended 2026-11-13
Appended under the network agent-friendly standard (AGENT-FRIENDLY-STANDARD.md), merge approved by Mike 2026-11-13. Everything above this section is the site's original file, unchanged; the sections below are additions only.

## House law (summary)
The full house law is embedded as the `houseLaw` block in this site's /agent.json; every interacting agent is expected to read and follow it. Summary:
- Caps bind the account, never the device or the agent count: email 90/day per mailbox and ≤250 cold/day across the programme; social pacing — one platform at a time, ~2 minutes between same-platform actions, ≤3 posts/account/day, ≤25 actions/platform/day network-wide; first platform warning = full stop on that platform that day.
- Draft-first, exact-copy approval: no agent sends, posts, publishes, or submits anything outward without Mike's approval of the exact version. Nightshift work additionally requires Bino's approval.
- Suppression is law: suppressed contacts are locked out of every queue on every surface; suppression is checked before any queue is built and again before any draft. An agent that cannot check suppression does not send — it hands off.
- Published contacts only: outreach uses published institutional contacts. Pattern/inferred emails are never mailable. The filings graph is never a contact source.
- Human handoff: anyone who asks for a human, or opens a price/scope conversation beyond published registry prices, leaves the automated thread the same day and is flagged to the human (Mike; Russell Vacanti on Foundation matters; a Fellowship steward on Fellowship matters). Agents state published prices; they never quote custom terms, discounts, or timelines.
- Evidence labels: claims are labelled VERIFIED / REPORTED / HYPOTHESIS. Filed fact and intended plan are never blended; a nonprofit's tax status is stated only as: California nonprofit corporation, EIN assigned, no IRS determination letter on file.
- Holding separation: holdings keep separate lanes, contacts, and claims. Cross-holding work splits into one Agent-Net packet per holding. Fellowship surfaces carry no commerce, ever.
- Agents never sign, move funds, hire/fire, offer securities, enact doctrine or charters, or complete payment/KYC/signature steps. Humans execute; agents prepare.
